_comment: Rulebook mechanics that Action NAMES reference but which are not glossary keywords (so they have no entry in keywords.json). Matched case-insensitively against an action's name/description so the app can explain them. Text is condensed from the verified digests in ../rules.

mechanics.name: Optical Camouflage
mechanics.basic: A hidden state. The unit is swapped for a camouflage marker that shows only roughly where it is.
points: A unit goes in with an Action that activates it, or may deploy already in it.
Going in removes its Hexagon Tokens, and it cannot gain a Highlight while hidden.
An attack on it must win a free Scan first. If the Scan fails, the attack fails.
Electronic Attacks need no Scan, and they leave the camouflage on.
It cannot Crush or Melee Lock anyone, but it can be Melee Locked.
mechanics.text:
A stealth state rather than a token. A unit enters it by performing an Action that activates Optical Camouflage, or by deploying straight into it (FAQ I6). On activation, swap the unit for its Optical Camouflage model and remove every Hexagon Token from it.

While camouflaged it cannot gain a Highlight Token, though it can still gain a Low Profile Token (FAQ I1). Activating it while already in Contact with an enemy does not Reveal it, because activating is not a Movement (FAQ I14). A camouflaged unit cannot Crush and cannot Melee Lock an enemy, but it can be Melee Locked (FAQ I3, I8, I9).

Any Melee, Firing or Explosion Damage attack aimed at it must Scan first. Designating it earns one free Scan: no Action Tick, the same procedure as the Common Action Scan, Silent, and at the attack's own range rather than 6 (FAQ I12, I18).

If the Scan fails the attack fails outright; the attacker still pays its own costs such as Ammo and Charge, and may use any Action Ticks it has left (FAQ I11). A unit whose Electronic Value is 0 or a dash cannot target it at all, because it cannot start the Scan counter-roll.

- Attacks that hit every unit in range need no Scan.
- Nor does an Electronic Attack, which leaves the camouflage on (FAQ I21).
- A Projectile Action designates a Landing Grid rather than the unit, so it makes no Scan (FAQ M16).
- A Mine still detonates on a camouflaged unit (FAQ I13).

The camouflage model marks only a suspected position, so the real unit may be elsewhere.

mechanics.name: Revealed
mechanics.basic: Leaving Optical Camouflage: the marker is swapped back for the unit, which then makes its Manifestation Movement. Any of these Reveals a hidden unit:
points: It performs the Reveal Common Action.
It performs an Action or a Maneuver without Silence. Turning on the spot counts.
A Movement by either unit ends with an enemy touching its base.
An enemy wins a Scan against it.
The Part that hid it is destroyed. Then it is Revealed where it stands, with no Manifestation Movement.
mechanics.text:
Leaving Optical Camouflage. Swap the camouflage model back for the unit model.

Four things reveal a unit and then let it make Manifestation Movement.
- The first is its own Reveal Common Action.
- The second is performing any Action that lacks the Silence keyword, the Action that activated the camouflage aside; Maneuvering counts, including a facing change with no movement, unless a Stealth Chassis gives the Maneuver Silence (FAQ I2).
- The third is any Movement, by either unit, that ends with an enemy in contact with its base (FAQ I4). That includes Forced Movement such as Crush, Drag, Knockback and a Taurus swap (FAQ I16, I23), and a Beacon or Mine launched, deployed or laid into contact (FAQ I10), but not a Missile. A camouflaged unit that moves onto a Mine is not revealed by it; the Mine detonates instead (FAQ I24, M19).
- The fourth is a successful enemy Scan.

Passive Actions and Interception do not reveal it, and neither does Forced Movement, which is Silent (FAQ E12); a Crush takes the Silence of the Movement that caused it (FAQ E13). A Pholcus landing from Flight Mode is a Move and reveals it before its blast (FAQ I19).

An Immobilized unit is revealed in place and cannot move (FAQ I20). When a revealing Action grants a follow-up attack, the unit reveals first, and the follow-up is forfeited if it can no longer attack the target (FAQ I22). Destroying the Part that performed the activating Action reveals it in place with no Manifestation Movement.

mechanics.name: Manifestation Movement
mechanics.basic: When a hidden unit is Revealed, it appears near its marker: anywhere within Range of it equal to its Stealth value.
points: Count the Range in Large Grids, orthogonally. Stealth 2 reaches 12 Grids, and Stealth 0 appears in place.
Units and terrain in between do not matter, but the unit must fit where it lands.
Its owner picks where it appears and which way it faces.
An Immobilized unit is Revealed in place.
If an attack Revealed it, the attack goes ahead only if the new position is still in the attack's Range, arc and line of sight.
mechanics.text:
The move a unit makes the instant it is Revealed. Because the Optical Camouflage model only marked a suspected position, the unit may appear anywhere within Range X of it, where X is the Stealth Value of the Action that activated the camouflage.

Range is counted in Large Grids along an orthogonal path (4.2.1), so Stealth 2 reaches 12 Grids and not the 24 of a 5 by 5 square; Stealth 0 means it appears where it stood.

It is Teleportation Movement following the Flying Movement rules, so terrain and units in between are ignored and it may land behind a high wall (FAQ I17). It must fit where it lands, a Ground Unit cannot land in an Abyss, and its player chooses its facing there. An Immobilized unit makes none (FAQ I20).

If the new position still meets every requirement of the incoming attack, its Range, its Forward Arc and its Line of Sight, the attack carries on from there; if it does not, the attack fails (FAQ I22).

mechanics.name: Scanning
mechanics.basic: A Scan uncovers a hidden enemy: it Reveals a unit in Optical Camouflage, or removes a Low Profile Token.
points: Every Mech has Scan: a Tactical, Short Action with Range 6.
Pick an enemy in Optical Camouflage or carrying a Low Profile Token, and make an Electronic Counter-roll against it.
Win, and a camouflaged enemy is Revealed, or its Low Profile Token comes off.
An attack on a camouflaged enemy makes a free Scan first. If the Scan fails, so does the attack.
A Scan is Silent, so a camouflaged unit can Scan without giving itself away.
mechanics.text:
Reveals enemy units in Optical Camouflage and strips Low Profile Tokens. Designate an enemy that is in Optical Camouflage or bearing a Low Profile Token, then make an Electronic Counter-roll as the Initiator with the unit's whole Electronic Value, every undestroyed Part counted (FAQ G3).

On success, camouflaged targets are Revealed (their own player then makes their Manifestation Movement), and Low Profile Tokens are removed. Only token-based Low Profile can be scanned away; Low Profile from an aura cannot (FAQ Q3).

Every Mech has Scan as a Common Action: Tactical, Short, Range 6, performed with the Torso. It is printed without Silence, but FAQ I18 says the Rules Supplement will make it Silent, so it is played as Silent. A Scan never uses a Repeater, which serves Electronic Attack and Electronic Support only.

Designating a camouflaged unit with a Firing or Melee Action earns one free Scan at no Action Tick, at the attack's own range, retried with a fresh attack if it fails (FAQ I11, I12, I18).

- An Electronic Attack needs no Scan (FAQ I21), nor does an attack on every unit in range or a Mine, and a Projectile Action gives none (FAQ M16).
- A unit with an Electronic Value of 0 or a dash cannot Scan, and Containers cannot be Scanned (FAQ I25).

The Hyena's and the Dragonfly's Scan Battlefield Scans every enemy it can change within its Range, one Counter-roll each.

mechanics.name: Electronic Counter-roll
mechanics.basic: How Electronic Warfare is decided: both units roll Yellow Dice equal to their Electronic Value, and the unit that started it must win.
points: More Lightning wins. On a tie, more Light Hits wins, and if that ties too, the Initiator wins.
A Mech's Electronic Value is the total of its undestroyed Parts.
Only Range matters: terrain and line of sight are ignored.
A unit with Electronic Value 0 cannot start one, and a unit printed with a dash cannot be targeted by one.
Each side counts hollow faces only if it is in Offensive Stance.
mechanics.text:
Both sides roll Yellow Dice equal to their Electronic Value, which for a Mech is the sum of all its undestroyed Parts (FAQ G3). The Initiator wins with more Lightning; if Lightning ties, more Light Hit, a double Light Hit counting two; if both tie, the Initiator still wins. The Initiator must win for the action's effect to apply.

Each side reads hollow faces by its own Stance, Offensive making them count, and a Shutdown unit gains none. Electronic Value 0 cannot initiate, and a unit printed with a dash cannot be the Responder (FAQ I25). Focus follows the order of any roll: the Initiator declares, then the Responder, then each rerolls (FAQ G4).

A Passive that triggers on a successful Counter-roll fires for its unit in either role. Electronic Support targets allies and needs no roll. An Electronic Attack is not an attack in the attack sequence's sense (FAQ G5), and it needs no Scan against a camouflaged unit (FAQ I21).

Modifiers:
- Strength +X adds X dice to the Initiator.
- Warfare Node X lets an ally within its range roll the node Mech's Electronic Value plus X.
- A Strength -1 aura takes a die off an enemy's roll.
- A Tarantula's Load lends its Electronic Value to the Mech it touches while that Mech performs an Action, never to the Carrier itself (FAQ O4, O5, O6, O7).
- Firewatch spends 1 Link to count Eyes as Lightning.
- A Repeater lends its position (FAQ G1, G2).

Electronic Warfare ignores Terrain and Line of Sight completely, so only Range matters.

mechanics.name: Reboot
mechanics.basic: How a Shutdown Mech comes back: it must Reboot at its next Action Opportunity.
points: A Shutdown Mech still sets a Timing Dial, and Reboots when that Timing comes round.
The Reboot restores 1 Link and puts the Mech in Defensive, Mobility or Offensive Stance.
Afterwards it has only 1 Action Tick, for one Action of its dial's Timing, and no Maneuver.
Link given back by an ally does not Reboot it.
mechanics.text:
The only Action a Shutdown Mech may take, and it must take it: a Mech in Shutdown Stance Reboots the next time it gains an Action Opportunity (FAQ K17). So it still sets a Timing Dial each round, and the dial decides when that is. A Mech shut down part-way through its own Opportunity Reboots at the start of its next one.

The Reboot restores 1 Link and changes the Stance to Defensive, Mobility or Offensive, never Shutdown. What is left of that Opportunity is 1 Action Tick, for one Action of the Timing on the dial: no Maneuver, no Extra Ticks, and no Starting Action exception such as Flexible Timing, CQC or Feint (4.1.1, FAQ L8).

Link restored to a Shutdown Mech by an ally, such as an Aurora's Strengthen Link, does not Reboot it (FAQ L3). An Extra Action Opportunity from Echoes is an Action Opportunity, so a Shutdown Mech with the Link to be chosen can Reboot in it (FAQ L8).

mechanics.name: Parry
mechanics.basic: A Melee-only defence: the defender picks a Part with a Parry Value to take the hit, and adds that many White dice to its Defense Roll.
points: Declare it when the hit location is chosen, before the Part Die is rolled.
No Parry in Shutdown or against a Back Attack.
A Parry that stops all the damage cancels the attack's On Hit effects.
A Drone with a Parry Value parries automatically in Melee, except against a Back Attack.
mechanics.text:
A melee-only defence. The defender designates a Part with a Parry Value as the target Part and adds that many White dice to the Defense Roll. It is declared at the hit-location step, before the Part Die, or not at all (FAQ C6).

- Not available while in Shutdown or against a Back Attack.
- If a Black Die still decides the Part - the attacker could designate too, as with Snipe - the Parry dice only apply when it matches (FAQ A14).
- A Parry that holds, with nothing Penetrating, cancels every [On Hit] effect of the attack (FAQ C5).
- A Drone with a Parry Value parries automatically in Melee, except against a Back Attack.
- Surplus Damage never gets Parry dice (4.8).

mechanics.name: Armor Piercing X
mechanics.basic: Armor Piercing X makes the target remove X White dice from its Defense Roll before rolling.
points: It removes dice, so it stacks with a Fragile Token.
A Defense Roll never drops below 1 White die.
It applies to the whole pool: Armor or Structure, Protection, Parry and aura dice.
It does not carry into Surplus Damage.
mechanics.text:
The target removes X White dice from its Defense Roll before rolling. The dice are removed rather than the result reduced, so the effect stacks with a Fragile Token, but the White dice of a Defense Roll can never be reduced below 1 (p.50): a Part left with a single die keeps it and rolls.

The removal applies to the whole pool: the Armor or Structure the Part rolls, any Terrain or Unit Protection, and any Parry or aura dice. It does not reach Surplus Damage, which inherits no Action effects (4.8).

The X is the number printed on the Action's own line. FPA-02 Spike's trait grants Armor Piercing 1 on every Firing Action, and that adds to any value the weapon prints.

mechanics.name: Focus
mechanics.basic: Spend 1 Link to reroll any dice of one roll, the Black Die included.
points: A Mech cannot spend its last Link on Focus.
The attacker declares first, then the defender; then each rerolls in the same order.
Only one reroll effect per roll, such as Focus or the Whistle, chosen when declaring.
In an Explosion or a Surplus Damage roll, only the defender may Focus.
mechanics.text:
Spend 1 Link to reroll any dice of one roll, including the Black Die that locates the Part (4.10). Focus may not be paid with a Mech's last Link (FAQ L1). Link lost to damage or effects can reach 0, at which point the Mech enters Shutdown Stance.

The order is fixed (4.4.1 step 5): the attacker declares, then the defender, then the attacker rerolls, then the defender, and an Electronic Counter-roll keeps the same order (FAQ G4). Each roll takes one reroll effect only (FAQ A6): Focus, a lent {Eye} reroll such as Guidance Support, or the Whistle, chosen at the declare.

In an Explosion or a Surplus Damage roll only the defender may Focus. A Mech in Shutdown has no pilot skills, so ZPA-39 Cadaver's free Focus does not apply there (FAQ L3).

mechanics.name: Movement and the Maneuver
mechanics.basic: A Mech moves with its Maneuver, up to its Maneuver Value in Grids, or with a Movement Action at that Action's Range.
points: Turning on the spot costs no Range, but it is Movement: it spends the Maneuver.
Any Movement in an Action Opportunity, a turn or a Shock Attack walk included, loses Stationary bonuses.
A Mech with a destroyed Chassis makes no Movement Action, and its Maneuver may only turn it.
Push moves the target in any straight line the pusher chooses, and a pushed Mech loses 1 Link.
Units that cannot move, such as Deployables, cannot be moved by any effect either.
mechanics.text:
Every Action Opportunity brings one Maneuver: the Mech may move up to its Maneuver Value in Grids, printed on its Chassis and doubled in Mobility Stance, and may change its Facing. A Movement Action moves at its own printed Range instead, or at the Maneuver Value where it prints none. Range is counted in orthogonal steps between Large Grids (4.2.1).

Flying Movement passes over terrain and Units and ends only where the Unit fits; a Flying Unit cannot Crush and is never Melee Locked (FAQ E1, E14). An Aerial Unit, such as a Missile, a Projectile or a Mine, is above the board: Units may stand under it, it is never Crushed, and Interception is what stops it. Teleportation, a Blink or a Manifestation, ignores everything between its two Grids.

Turning on the spot costs no Movement Range, but it is still Movement: it is a Maneuver of its own and spends the Maneuver Tick, and a Movement Action may be spent on a turn alone (FAQ E3, E18). [Stationary] asks whether the unit performed any Movement in its Action Opportunity, so a turn, a Shock Attack walk or a free move after an Action loses it (FAQ K24). Being moved by someone else does not (ruled 2026-09-25).

A Mech whose Chassis is destroyed cannot perform Movement Actions, a Jump or a Blink included, and its Maneuver may only change its Facing (4.3.4; FAQ E4). An Immobilized Unit cannot Maneuver or perform Movement Actions at all, turning included, unless the Action is Unstoppable (6.3.2). A Non-humanoid Movement Action costs Link to perform, and never the last Link (FAQ L1).

- Shock Attack X: before performing the Action, the Unit may move up to X Grids.
- Push X: the pushing player moves the target X Grids in any straight direction they choose, a pushed Mech loses 1 Link, and the pusher does not follow. Otherwise it follows the Knockback X rules.
- Forced Movement (Knockback, Push, a Drag, a tow or a Crush) is never voluntary: Melee Lock and Break Away do not apply, and a Unit that cannot move, such as a Deployable, cannot be Force-Moved at all (4.3.4).

mechanics.name: Crush
mechanics.basic: A Large unit can push through a smaller one by moving into its Grid. Its Movement ends there.
points: Only Large units on the ground Crush, and only smaller units, allies included. Flying and camouflaged units cannot.
The victim moves 1 Grid, into any Grid around it except the one the mover is coming from.
With nowhere to go it swaps places with the mover. One that can never move, like a Beacon, is destroyed.
The crushing player chooses where each victim goes and which way it faces.
The Movement ends there, Straight Line range or not. Aerial units, Mines and Barricades are never Crushed.
mechanics.text:
Only a Large (3x3) Ground Unit can Crush, and only Units smaller than itself, allies included (FAQ E7), unless a trait such as Indomitable says otherwise. Only Basic Movement Crushes: never Flying Movement (FAQ E14), Teleportation or Forced Movement (4.3.4), and never a Unit in Optical Camouflage (FAQ I3, I9). Aerial Units, Mines among them, are passed over: Units may be placed above them. Barricades and walls are never Crushed (FAQ E6).

Moving into an occupied Grid forces a Crush, resolved as the Unit is about to enter it. Each crushed Unit undergoes Forced Movement of 1 Grid, into any of the Grids around it except the one the crushing Unit is entering from, which it is still standing in (p.47). The crushing player chooses the Grid and the Facing (FAQ L6).

- A crushed Unit with none of those Grids open exchanges positions with the crushing Unit instead, taking the Grid it is vacating.
- A Unit that cannot be moved at all, such as a Deployable like a Beacon, is destroyed outright, and its destruction scores like any other.
- Destructible Terrain in the Grid is destroyed.
- The crushing Unit still pays Break Away on the way in (FAQ E22).
- It then enters the Grid, and its Movement ends there at once, even with Straight Line range left (FAQ E16).

A Firefly in Low Profile or Optical Camouflage may pass through smaller Units and Containers on its way, but a Crush only happens where its Movement ends (FAQ I15; ruled 2026-09-25). A move The Red Shoes controls may end in a Crush, and the controlling player places the victims.

mechanics.name: Penetration
mechanics.basic: Penetration is damage getting through: any Heavy or Light Hit left after the Defense Roll damages the target.
points: A Part with no Structure Value is Destroyed at once.
Otherwise each Penetration moves the Part one step: Intact, then Damaged, then Destroyed.
A Damaged Part rolls its Structure Value instead of its Armor Value to defend.
Damage stopped by Defense dice is still a Hit, so On Hit effects apply; damage stopped by a Dodge is not.
mechanics.text:
After Damage Resolution, any Heavy Hit or Light Hit left unoffset causes Penetration on the target Unit or Part. A Part with no Structure Value is Destroyed at once. A Part with a Structure Value takes a Damaged Token, or is Destroyed if it already had one: Intact to Damaged to Destroyed, one step per Penetration whatever the amount of damage. While Damaged, a Part rolls its Structure Value instead of its Armor Value for Defense dice.

A Hit and a Penetration are separate: damage offset by Defense is a Hit with no Penetration, so [On Hit] effects such as Knockback still apply, while damage offset by Dodge is neither. Concussion is not an [On Hit] effect: like every Lightning effect it fires on each {Lightning} no Dodge cancelled, Penetration or not.

mechanics.name: Surplus Damage
mechanics.basic: Once a Penetration happens, any leftover Hits are Surplus Damage. It only matters if the attack has a Surplus Damage keyword.
points: The keywords are Mutilation, Cleaving and Scatter-shot; with several, the attacker picks one.
The Surplus roll gets no Attack Roll, Protection, Parry or Armor Piercing.
Only the defender may Focus, and the defender cannot choose the hit location.
On Hit effects come from the first hit only.
mechanics.text:
Once a Penetration has occurred, every Heavy Hit and Light Hit still unoffset is Surplus Damage. On its own it does nothing. It is resolved only when the Action carries a Surplus Damage keyword (Mutilation, Cleaving or Scatter-shot), per Section 4.8; with several such keywords the Attacker chooses one. A keyword granted under a condition, such as [Two-Handed] or [Charged], counts only when the condition holds.

The Surplus roll makes no Attack Roll and gets no Terrain, Unit Protection or Parry dice, nor the attacker's Armor Piercing; only the defender may Focus, and the defender cannot choose the hit location (FAQ A27). No Action effect fires from it: the attack's [On Hit] effects come from the first hit alone.

A target destroyed by the first hit can still be Cleaved past into another Unit (FAQ D4, D12).

mechanics.name: Integrity Loss
mechanics.basic: A Mech left with 2 or fewer Parts suffers Integrity Loss: it is removed in that round's End Phase.
points: It keeps acting normally until then.
Destroying the Torso kills the Mech at once instead.
Every other Part destroyed costs the Mech 1 Link, and at 0 Link it drops into Shutdown.
The kill goes to the last unit that destroyed one of its Parts.
mechanics.text:
A Mech reduced to 2 or fewer remaining Parts suffers Integrity Loss. It still acts as normal for the rest of the Round in which that happened, then is removed during that Round's End Phase, before Token Management and scoring, and the kill is credited to the last unit that reduced its Part count (FAQ P4).

Destroying the Torso is different and kills the unit outright. Every other Part destroyed flips its card face-down, stops counting toward any Value, and costs 1 Link, and a Mech whose Link reaches 0 drops straight into Shutdown Stance. A Repaired Part that is hit is removed at once, with no Defense Roll and no second Link loss, and the hit goes to the Torso (FAQ J23).

mechanics.name: Break Away
mechanics.basic: A unit next to an enemy with a Melee Action is Melee Locked: it cannot fire, and walking away costs extra.
points: Any Adjacent enemy with a Melee Action and line of sight to it Locks it. A Repaired Part still counts.
A Locked unit cannot perform Firing Actions unless they have Melee Firing. It may still Intercept.
Leaving a Grid while Locked costs 1 extra Movement for each enemy Locking it at that moment.
A Panzer pilot charges 1 more, which may be paid with 1 Link instead, never the last.
Flying units cannot be Locked. A camouflaged unit can be, but Locks nobody. Forced Movement pays no extra.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook 4.3.5; FAQ E2, E5, E22, I8, J23, L1, N3
mechanics.text:
A Unit is Melee Locked by an enemy that has a Melee Action it could perform, is Adjacent to it and has line of sight to it (4.3.5). Extended Melee does not stretch the Lock past Adjacent. A Repaired Part can still perform Actions, so it locks like any other (FAQ J23). A Mech in Shutdown or in Cruise Mode locks nobody (FAQ N3), and nor does a Unit in Optical Camouflage, though it can be Melee Locked itself (FAQ I8).

A Flying Unit, a Transformable Mech in Cruise Mode among them, and a Unit making Flying Movement cannot be Melee Locked. A Melee Locked Unit cannot perform Firing Actions unless the Action carries Melee Firing. It may still Intercept: 4.3.5 bans Firing Actions, the Fire Control Interference Token names Interception separately, and the figure on p.67 shows a Locked Unit intercepting (ruled 2026-09-25).

Break Away: when a Locked Unit makes Basic Movement, each time it exits a Grid while Locked it pays 1 additional Movement Range for every Unit locking it at that moment. A Crush pays it too (FAQ E22), a turn on the spot is free (FAQ E5), and a Crawl cannot Break Away at all. Flying Movement ignores Melee Lock, and Forced Movement never triggers it (FAQ E2).

Obstruct, the Panzer pilot's trait, makes that 2 for a Grid it locks. The extra 1 may be paid with 1 Link instead, step by step and locker by locker, but a Mech never spends its last Link (FAQ L1; ruled 2026-09-25).

mechanics.name: Ammo and Charge
mechanics.basic: Two kinds of token on an Action: Ammo limits how often it can be used, and Charge powers up one use.
points: Each Ammo icon is a token. Flip one per use; when all are spent, the Action cannot be used.
A Projectile Action spends 1 Ammo for each Projectile placed.
The Charge Action (Tactical, Short, Silent) turns one Part's Charge Token face-up.
A Charged Part stays Charged until an Action consumes it, which is always optional.
An attack that fails still spends its Ammo and Charge.
mechanics.text:
Two separate token economies printed as icons on an Action.

Ammo caps how many times an Action can be used: place one face-up Ammo Token per Ammo Icon at deployment, flip one face-down per use, and once they are all spent the Action cannot be performed (4.13). A Projectile Action consumes its Ammo as each Projectile is placed, one per Projectile, so Volley X can spend X (4.7).

An attack that fails, such as one on a camouflaged unit whose Scan fails, still consumes its Ammo and Charge (4.12.2). Some Actions replenish Ammo by naming a Unit or Part and flipping consumed tokens back face-up, never above the starting number, and repairing a Part does not restore its Ammo (FAQ J15).

Charge is a one-shot state instead. The token starts face-down, and the Charge Action, a Tactical Short Action with Silence (6.1), flips one named Part's token face-up: one Part per Charge Action, and a Part already Charged cannot be Charged again until it is spent (4.14, FAQ H1, H3). A Mech with two Parts that can be Charged may perform two Charge Actions in one Opportunity, one for each Part (FAQ H6, H7), and one with nothing left to Charge cannot perform it at all (FAQ H2).

An Action with a Charge-conditional effect may consume the token by flipping it back down, and never has to, even as an Automatic Action (FAQ H4, H8). KC Armor needs a consumed Charge, is declared after the unit is targeted and before the Hit Location Die (FAQ H5, H9), and holds through Surplus Damage (FAQ D11).

When a Part is Discarded or Disarmed, its Ammo and Charge carry to the Discard Card only for an Action there that uses them, and are otherwise removed (4.17).

A Missile Group is one Launch and one Ammo Token for its X Units (6.2).

mechanics.name: Scream
mechanics.basic: The Roaring Eagle Drone's Electronic Attack against every enemy Mech in Range at once.
points: Tactical, Automatic, Range 4.
It makes one Electronic Counter-roll against each enemy Mech in Range, with Strength +1 (one extra die).
Each win takes 1 Link from that Mech, and a Mech left at 0 Link goes into Shutdown.
Terrain and line of sight do not matter, only Range.
mechanics.text:
Scream is the Action of the ZHDR-205 Roaring Eagle Drone, not a keyword: Tactical, Automatic, Range 4, an Electronic Attack against every enemy Mech within its Range, one Electronic Counter-roll each, with Strength +1 on the Drone's side. Each success takes 1 Link from that Mech.

Like all Electronic Warfare it ignores Terrain and Line of Sight and is limited only by Range. Link lost this way can reach 0, which puts the Mech into Shutdown Stance (4.10).

mechanics.name: Remote Access
mechanics.basic: In the Terminals missions, every Mech can take a Terminal with an Electronic Counter-roll.
points: Remote Access: in the End Phase, a Short Tactic with Range 4, performed with the Torso.
Roll against the Terminal's Electronic Value of 3; win, and the Terminal is accessed.
Direct Access: in the End Phase, a side with a Mech (not in Shutdown) or a Drone in the zone, and no enemy there, takes it.
Each Terminal can be accessed once per round.
mechanics.text:
A Universal Action every Mech has in the Terminals missions (5.3.3). Performed in the End Phase with the Torso, Range 4, as a Short Tactic: make an Electronic Counter-roll against the Terminal, whose Electronic Value is 3; success accesses it.

Direct Access is the other way: at the End Phase a Terminal is accessed by a side with a Mech outside Shutdown Stance or a Drone inside its Tactical Zone and no enemy Unit there.

A Terminal can be accessed once per Round; its token is flipped face-down when taken and every Terminal token is flipped back face-up at the End Phase.

mechanics.name: Detonation
mechanics.basic: How a Projectile delivers its payload. It attacks a unit or a Grid, and a Projectile that Detonates is destroyed.
points: A Projectile acts as it lands, in the Delay Phase, or all the time, as its Action says.
It targets what its card names: a free pick among enemies, the nearest where printed, a named Unit type first.
Destructible Terrain in Range is always a choice. With no target at all it is destroyed, unless its card says otherwise.
A Missile flies to its target first, and that flight can be Intercepted.
Explosion damage needs no sight or facing, allows no Protection, and each unit caught rolls on its own.
mechanics.text:
Every Projectile Action puts a Projectile on the board, and the Projectile then acts on its own (4.7.4). An Immediate Action resolves the moment it lands. A Delayed Action resolves in the Delay Phase, when the Projectile is designated in turn (3.6). A Passive one is always on, or fires on a trigger such as a unit entering a Mine's Grid.

Target choice (4.7.5):
- "Target 1 Enemy Unit" is a free pick among the enemies in Range.
- "The nearest Unit" follows that rule, as the Unfolded Pholcus does (FAQ M18).
- A Unit Type the card names comes first while one is in Range, then any other: the PK3 takes an Enemy Mech before anything else.
- Destructible Terrain in Range is always a legal target unless the card says otherwise, and a Neutral target is never forced on a Missile (FAQ M12).
- A Missile Group's Units attack one target: the first Unit designated picks it, and the rest follow (p.94).

A Projectile whose Delayed Action needs a target, and finds none in Range when it is designated, is destroyed unless its card says otherwise (4.7.5). The PK3 prints that it is not removed then (GoF 1.021). A Deployable whose Delayed Action is not a Detonation, such as a Link Beacon, stays and acts again each Delay Phase.

A Missile flies from its Landing Point into its target's Grid before it Detonates, and that flight is Movement: the enemies in Range of either end Intercept it (p.67, 4.9). A Missile Group's Units are Intercepted one by one.

Optical Camouflage (p.71): a Projectile that targets a Unit and has an Electronic Value Scans a camouflaged target first, as the Initiator, and one with no Electronic Value cannot pick it. After the Reveal the Explosion follows only if the target is still in Range (FAQ M16). One that attacks every Unit in its Range needs no Scan, and a failed Scan still spends the Projectile.

Explosion damage (4.7.6) needs no line of sight or facing, the defender claims no Terrain or Unit Protection, and only the defender may Focus. A Projectile never makes a Back Attack, though against a Shutdown target it designates the Part hit (FAQ M4).

An attack on every Unit in Range hits allies too, and each Unit caught makes its own Attack and Defense Rolls (FAQ M21). Allied Missiles targeting a Unit near an allied Rumba Beacon may reroll {Eye} (FAQ M25). A Projectile that Detonates is destroyed.

mechanics.name: Victory Points and winning
mechanics.basic: Victory Points (VP) decide the game.
points: Take VP tokens as they are earned.
At the end of the game, the side with more VP wins.
On a tie, the side with more Mech Parts and Drones still on the board wins.
mechanics.text: Track Victory Points with VP tokens as they are earned. At the end of the game the side with more VP wins. If VP are equal, the winner is the side with more Mech Parts and Drones still on the board.

mechanics.name: Main Task Cards
mechanics.basic: The Main Task is the mission both sides play for, and it also sets both deployment zones.
points: In setup, draw 3 Main Task Cards; each side discards 1, and the last card is the mission.
The card shows the Tactical Areas, both deployment zones, the task, its Victory Points and the Task Item Tokens used.
mechanics.text:
The Main Task sets the encounter objective and also prints both deployment zones. During setup draw 3 Main Task Cards, each side discards 1, and the remaining card is the mission.

A card shows the Tactical Areas in play, both deployment zones (for example Black 3x5 and White 3x5 strips on opposite edges), the task text, the VP values, and which Task Item Tokens are used.

mechanics.name: Secondary Task Cards
mechanics.basic: Each player also picks a Secondary Task for extra Victory Points, and shows it to the other player.
points: Pick during setup, the First Player first.
Some score through one of your own Mechs: Escort, Weapons Test and Disposal Procedure.
Some target an enemy Mech: Behead and Bounty Hunt.
The rest score by how the battle goes: Annihilation, Mercy and Excavation Claim.
mechanics.text:
Starting with the First Player, each player picks 1 Secondary Task during setup and shows it to the other player (5.2.1). The core box has 8.

- Three designate one of your own Mechs: Escort scores 3 VP if it survives, Weapons Test scores 1 VP each time it destroys a Part or a Drone, and Disposal Procedure scores 2 VP when it is destroyed.
- Two target the enemy: Behead is worth 5 VP and your opponent names which of their Mechs is the target; Bounty Hunt is worth 4 VP and you name it.
- Annihilation scores 2 VP per enemy Mech and 1 VP per Drone destroyed, Mercy scores 2 VP for destroying no enemy Mech, and Excavation Claim scores 2 VP if only your Units stand in a Tactical Zone you designate at the end of the game (Low Value Units do not count).

The English text is a translation of the printed cards.

mechanics.name: Tactics Cards
mechanics.basic: Tactics Cards are one-use commander actions, bought with squad points.
points: Each costs 30 points, and a squad may take at most one copy of each.
Each player may play only 1 per round, and a used card is gone for the game.
They are not bound by the faction rule, so any squad may take any of them.
mechanics.text:
Six Tactics Cards come in the core box, each costing 30 points against the squad total: Additional Instructions and Battlefield Recovery (GoF), Hit and Run and Tactical Disposition (UN), System Repair and Remote Restart (RDL). They are bought during list building, one copy of each at most (FAQ P2).

Each player may play only 1 Tactics Card per round, and a card once used is discarded for the rest of the game. A Tactics Card is an action the commander takes rather than a Unit (5.4.2), so it is not bound by the faction rule that applies to Units and Parts.

mechanics.name: Ticks and the Action Opportunity
mechanics.basic: Each Action Opportunity gives a Mech 1 Maneuver Tick and 2 Action Ticks to spend.
points: A Maneuver costs the Maneuver Tick. A Short Action costs 1 Action Tick, a Medium 2, and a Long all three Ticks.
Maneuver first: once an Action Tick is spent, the Maneuver Tick is gone.
The first Action must match the Timing on the dial.
Each Action on a Part can be used once per Opportunity.
mechanics.text:
Every time a Mech receives an Action Opportunity it generates 1 Maneuver Tick and 2 Action Ticks. A Maneuver costs the Maneuver Tick, a Short Action costs 1 Action Tick, a Medium costs 2, and a Long costs the Maneuver Tick plus both Action Ticks, which is why a Long Action rules out Maneuvering. An Action that needs more Ticks than remain when it is declared cannot be performed.

Ticks are consumed in order: once any Action Tick has gone the Maneuver Tick can no longer be used, so a Maneuver has to come first.

The first Action of the Opportunity is the Starting Action and its Action Type must match the Timing on the dial, unless Flexible Timing, CQC or Feint says otherwise; later Actions in the same Opportunity have no type restriction. With no valid Starting Action declared, no other Short Action may be performed in that Opportunity either (3.4.3, Note 2). Each Action on a Part may only be performed once per Opportunity. The Opportunity ends when its Ticks are consumed or forfeited (3.4.4).

After a Reboot a Mech has only 1 Action Tick (4.1.1). Overload, Attack Mode and Hammerhead Domestic Expert add ordinary Action Ticks to the pool, which combine freely but never let an Action repeat (FAQ K14). Extra Ticks are separate: they may only be used after every base Tick is consumed, never combine with a base Tick to pay for one Action, only pay for their own Action Type when one is named, and may repeat an Action already performed.

mechanics.name: Extra Ticks
mechanics.basic: An Extra Tick is a bonus Tick from a Part, spent at the end of the Opportunity on one Short Action.
points: Use it only after the Maneuver Tick and both Action Ticks are spent.
It pays for one Short Action on its own, never together with another Tick.
It may repeat an Action already performed this Opportunity.
If the grant names an Action type, it pays only for that type.
A Mech that has just Rebooted gets none.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook 3.4.5; FAQ K4, K6, K13, K14, K24, L8
mechanics.text:
An Extra Tick pays for one Short Action on its own, and never combines with a base Tick to pay for one Action (3.4.5). Two Extra Ticks never combine to pay for a Medium Action either (FAQ K14). It may only be used after the Maneuver Tick and both Action Ticks are consumed (3.4.5), at the end of the Opportunity, and it may repeat an Action already performed in it (FAQ K6); where the grant names an Action Type it pays only for that type.

A grant's condition is read when the Tick is spent. The Tempest core grants its Firing Tick only while the Mech is Stationary, and Stationary covers the whole Opportunity, so a Mech that moved at any point in it has lost the Tick (FAQ K24). The Glacier core grants its Tick when the Timing Dial is set to Firing, whatever the Starting Action (FAQ K13), and that holds in an Extra Action Opportunity too, because the dial is still set (FAQ K4).

A Mech that Reboots has none: the Reboot leaves 1 Action Tick and nothing more (FAQ L8).

mechanics.name: Overload
mechanics.basic: The OCSP Overloading Pack turns Link into Action Ticks: up to 2 Link, 1 Tick each.
points: Declare it at the start of the Opportunity, before any Maneuver or Action.
These are ordinary Action Ticks, so two of them can pay for a Medium Action.
They never let an Action repeat.
The Link is spent whether the Ticks are used or not, and never the last Link.
A destroyed Pack cannot Overload; a Repaired one can.
mechanics.ref: OCSP Overloading Pack, card 090; FAQ K10, K11, K14, K20, L1
mechanics._match_note: Deliberately English-only. The Chinese 超载 also appears in XTC's 超载注入, an unrelated Electronic Attack, and the Pack's own Action carries the English name so nothing is lost.
mechanics.text:
The OCSP Overloading Pack lets a Mech consume up to 2 Link at the start of its Action Opportunity, gaining 1 Action Tick for each point spent. It is declared at the beginning, before any Maneuver or Action, never part-way through (FAQ K10).

These are ordinary Action Ticks rather than Extra Ticks: they may be split between Actions as the Mech likes (FAQ K11), two of them pay for one Medium Action, which no pair of Extra Ticks can do, and they never let an Action repeat, so an Overloaded Mech may perform a Short, a Medium and a different Short Action (FAQ K14). Ticks are still consumed in order, so a Maneuver must come before the first Action Tick is spent (FAQ K20).

The Link is spent whether or not the Ticks are used, but never the last one, which cannot be spent voluntarily (4.10, FAQ L1): 2 Link buys one Tick and 3 buys two. The Pack must be intact to Overload through, since a destroyed Part's Action cannot be performed (3.4.3); a Repaired one still can. This Part cannot be used as a Load.

mechanics.name: Extra Action Opportunity
mechanics.basic: A whole extra turn for a Mech, granted by the Echoes Support Backpack.
points: The Mech gets a fresh Maneuver Tick, 2 Action Ticks, any Extra Ticks, and may change Stance.
Coordinate (Tactical, Medium, Range 4) grants it to another ally Mech, which loses 1 Link and needs at least 2.
The echoed Mech acts at once, then the granting Mech carries on.
Its first Action must match its own Timing Dial.
mechanics.ref: Echoes Support Backpack, card 009; FAQ K1, K3, K4, K7, K8, K19, K21, L8
mechanics.text:
A complete Action Opportunity, not an extra Tick: the Mech gets a fresh Maneuver Tick, two fresh Action Ticks, any Extra Tick its Parts grant (FAQ K4), and the chance to change Stance (FAQ K1).

The Echoes Support Backpack's Coordinate, a Tactical Medium Action of the granting Mech, grants one to a chosen Ally Mech other than itself within Range 4, and that Mech loses 1 Link; it must hold at least 2 Link to be chosen. A Mech acting in an Echoes Opportunity cannot use Echoes on another Mech during it (FAQ K3).

It happens immediately, inside the granting Mech's Opportunity: the echoed Mech acts, then the granting Mech continues (FAQ K21).
- The echoed Mech's Starting Action must match its own Timing, not the granter's (FAQ K7).
- A Mech echoed before its own activation still takes that activation (FAQ K19).
- A Mech may gain several Extra Opportunities from several Echoes Packs while it has the Link (FAQ K8).
- A Shutdown Mech given one Reboots in it, because it is an Action Opportunity (FAQ L8).

mechanics.name: On Hit
mechanics.basic: On Hit effects happen whenever an attack Hits, even if no damage gets through.
points: Any damage not stopped by a Dodge is a Hit.
Damage stopped by Defense dice still counts as a Hit.
A Parry that holds cancels every On Hit effect.
Lightning effects such as Concussion are separate: each Lightning not Dodged fires them.
mechanics.text:
[On Hit] effects apply when the attack Hits, which is a lower bar than Penetration. A Hit is any damage the defender did not offset with a Dodge. Defense dice offset Light Hits only, so damage stopped by Defense still counts as a Hit and the [On Hit] effect applies even though nothing got through. Damage offset by a Dodge is not a Hit.

A Parry that holds cancels every [On Hit] effect of the attack (FAQ C5, B2). Lightning effects such as Concussion are not [On Hit] effects: they fire on each {Lightning} no Dodge cancelled.

mechanics.name: Stance as a condition
mechanics.basic: Text marked with a Stance in brackets, such as [Offensive Stance], works only while the Mech is in that Stance.
points: The Stance is checked as the Action is performed.
A Mech picks Defensive, Mobility or Offensive at the start of each of its own Opportunities.
Offensive counts hollow attack icons, Defensive counts hollow defence icons, and Mobility adds Dodge dice and doubles the Maneuver.
Shutdown is never chosen: a Mech falls into it at 0 Link, and only a Reboot ends it.
A Drone keeps the Stance printed on its card.
mechanics.text:
An Action that names a Stance in brackets only applies that part of its text while the Mech is in that Stance, checked as the Action is performed. A Mech chooses its Stance at the start of each of its own Action Opportunities, before it Maneuvers or acts (4.1), and only Defensive, Mobility or Offensive may be chosen (3.4.2).

The Stance lasts until changed: Offensive converts hollow attack icons to solid, Defensive converts hollow defence icons to solid, and Mobility adds Dodge dice and doubles the Maneuver.

Shutdown is never chosen. A Mech falls into it at 0 Link, or when an effect forces it, as the Lightning of the Valkyrie and the Harpy can, and only a Reboot takes it out again. A Shutdown Mech may do nothing but Reboot and gains no benefit when rolling. When it is the target of an Action the attacker designates the Part, and no Part ability such as Parry defends it. It triggers nothing of its own, Passive effects and pilot skills included (4.1, FAQ L3); Anser alone is the exception (FAQ L5).

A Drone keeps the Stance printed on its card and cannot be switched out of it (FAQ O2). An Action's Stance change, such as Suppression, happens before the Attack Roll.

A White Dwarf Bit changes Stance by turning its card over, and keeps every Token on it (FAQ N8).

mechanics.name: Low Value Units
mechanics.basic: A Low Value Unit is a minor piece: every Projectile, and every Drone printed with the Low Value tag.
points: It is not part of the Squad: it has no Points Value and is never placed during Deployment.
It cannot interact with Task Items, so it takes no Control Zone and accesses no Terminal.
It is worth no Victory Points when destroyed, its own detonation included.
It cannot gain Hexagon Tokens such as Highlight, though Auras still reach it.
It can still deny a Zone, since a Zone is held only with no enemy unit inside.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook p.82, 5.1; Rules Supplement 1.6; FAQ J3, M8, M15, M17, M23
mechanics.text:
Low Value Units are not part of the Squad and have no Points Value (p.82). Every Projectile is one (5.1), and so is every Drone printed with the Low Value tag: the SU1 and SU2 swarms, the White Dwarf's Bits, the Dragonfly, the KK9, the Delphinium and the Unfolded Pholcus. They arrive when a card puts them down, never at Deployment.

A Low Value Unit may not interact with a Task Item and is worth no Victory Points when destroyed, its own detonation included (FAQ M8). Taking a Control Zone or accessing a Terminal is interacting with a Task Item, so it can do neither (FAQ M15). Blocking is not: a Zone is held only if no enemy Units are present, so a Low Value Unit still denies it. The Excavation Claim card prints its own exclusion.

It cannot gain Hexagon Tokens, so it never bears Highlight (Rules Supplement 1.6; FAQ J3, M23), though Auras still reach it: allied Missiles and Mines near an MES Beacon share its Low Profile (FAQ M17).

mechanics.name: Automatic and Command Actions
mechanics.basic: The boxed icon beside a Drone Action's name says when it happens: by itself, on a Command, or always.
points: An Automatic Action {!} resolves by itself in the Automatic Phase, and a Drone with a target must take it.
A Command Action {?} happens when the Drone is given a Command: it then moves or performs that one Action.
An Action with no box is Passive, and always on.
A Drone takes one Command per Phase, and keeps the Stance printed on its card.
A commanded Drone still performs its Automatic Actions later in the round.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook 3.2, 3.5, 4.1, 4.15; FAQ A21, N8, O1, O2, O14; ruling I4
mechanics.text:
Every Action on a Drone card is marked with a boxed icon beside its name that says when it happens.
- {!} is an Automatic Action: it resolves by itself in the Automatic Phase, and Automatic Actions are obligatory (3.5): a Drone with a legal target must take it (ruling I4).
- {?} is a Command Action: it happens when the Drone is given a Command.
- An Action with neither box is Passive and is always on.

A Command comes three ways: a Command Token spent in the Command Phase (3.2.2), a Command Coordination later in the round (4.15.3), or the Additional Instructions Tactics Card (FAQ O14). A commanded Drone acts at once and either moves or performs one Command Action. A Drone moves only on a Command, never in the Automatic Phase. It takes one Command per Phase (FAQ O1), and one bearing a Command Token cannot take another (FAQ N8).

The Automatic Phase alternates like the Command Phase: the players take turns activating their Drones, each performing its Automatic Action, until both pass (3.5.1). A Drone that took a Command still performs its Automatic Actions, since the two phases are separate activations. A Drone keeps the Stance printed on its card and cannot be switched out of it (FAQ O2).

A Command Token given to a Drone is removed when the Command Phase ends (3.2.3). A Mech's own unspent tokens stay until the End Phase (4.15).

mechanics.name: Command Tokens
mechanics.basic: Mechs make Command Tokens and spend them to give Drones orders.
points: Each Mech makes 1 face-up Command Token at the start of the Command Phase, or more with Command Generation.
The players take turns giving Commands, and a player who passes gives no more that phase.
A Command lays the token face-down on an ally Drone, which moves or performs one Command Action at once.
A Mech's unspent tokens stay for Command Coordination or for Actions that use one, until the End Phase.
The Additional Instructions card gives a Drone one more Command Action, without a token.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook 3.2, 4.15; FAQ A21, N8, O1, O14; GoF 1.021; ruling I1

mechanics.name: Activation order in the Action Phase
mechanics.basic: Mechs act one at a time, in the order set by their Timing Dials.
points: The Timings go Swift, Melee, Projectile, Firing, Movement, Tactical.
Within one Timing, the lowest Initiative Value on the dial goes first.
On a full tie, the First Player's Mech goes first, then the sides alternate.
Every Mech sets a dial, a Shutdown one too, because that is when it Reboots.
mechanics.text:
Mechs act one at a time in Timing order, which never changes: Swift, Melee, Projectile, Firing, Movement, Tactical. Within one Timing the Pilot with the LOWEST Initiative Value at that Timing acts first, that number being the one printed under the Timing icon on the dial.

If two Mechs share both the Timing and the Initiative Value, the First Player's Mech goes first and the sides then alternate until every Mech at that value has acted. Which of one squad's tied Mechs takes each of its turns is that squad's choice, as in the Automatic and Delay Phases; the rulebook orders only the squads, so this is a reading rather than a printed rule.

Every Mech sets a dial, a Shutdown one included, because it Reboots when its Timing comes round (FAQ K17). An Extra Action Opportunity is taken at once, inside the granting Mech's own, and the granter then continues (FAQ K21).

mechanics.name: Token duration colours
mechanics.basic: A token's background colour says how long it lasts.
points: Green stays until something removes it.
Yellow flips to its reverse, usually red, at the end of the round.
Red is removed at the end of the round.
So a yellow token lasts two rounds.
mechanics.text:
The background colour of a Square or Hexagon Token says how long it lasts (2.5.3).
- Green stays until an Action or effect removes it.
- Yellow is flipped to its reverse at the end of the round; the reverse is usually red.
- Red is removed at the end of the round.

So a yellow token lasts two rounds: it flips at the first End Phase and comes off at the second. The Low Profile Token is green on its face and red on its reverse. Fragile, Fire Control Interference, Immobilized and Highlight are yellow on their face and red on their reverse.

mechanics.name: Deployment
mechanics.basic: How the squads are placed before the first round.
points: Both players roll 2 dice; the side with more Hits is the First Player and picks the board edge.
The First Player places one Unit in its Deployment Zone, then the players alternate one at a time.
Once one side has placed everything, the other places the rest.
A Mech picks its Stance as it is placed, and a unit able to activate Optical Camouflage may deploy already in it.
mechanics.text:
Before the first round both players roll 2 dice; the side with more Hits is the First Player and chooses which board edge to play from (3.1.2). A tie is rolled again.

The First Player deploys one Unit wholly within an unoccupied Grid of its Deployment Zone, then the players alternate one Unit at a time; once one side has placed everything, the other places all its remaining Units (3.1.4).

A Mech chooses its Stance as it is deployed and is Offensive if none is set. A Unit able to activate Optical Camouflage may be deployed directly into it.

mechanics.name: Interception
mechanics.basic: Interception shoots down enemy Missiles and other Aerial units as they are Launched or move.
points: Intercept X gives an Action X Interception Tokens for the whole game. Spent ones never come back.
A Launch, or an enemy Aerial unit's move, owes an attempt from each unit with its start or end Grid in Range.
It is not a choice: while an attempt can be made it must be, again and again until the Tokens run out or the target dies.
It is a Firing Action, so Smoke stops it and Firing bonuses apply, but it needs no arc and the target gets no Protection.
Deploying or Laying a Projectile owes none, and allied Projectiles are never Intercepted.
mechanics.text:
Intercept X on an Action puts X Interception Tokens on that Card at Deployment, and they are never restored (FAQ M27). An attempt is owed when an enemy Aerial Unit Moves or is Launched and either its starting Grid or its ending Grid is within the Action's Range (4.9). Only those two Grids count, never the path between (FAQ M9). Forced Movement and Teleportation of an enemy Aerial Unit count the same way (ruled 2026-09-26).

What triggers it:
- A Launch: a Projectile is Aerial at both ends of it whatever it is, a Beacon included (4.7.2, FAQ M20). Deploy and Lay never trigger it.
- Aerial Drones and Mechs, when they move (FAQ O11, O15), and a Missile's flight into its target's Grid in the Delay Phase (p.67).
- Never an allied Projectile (FAQ M1).

Interception is mandatory (FAQ M5): while its conditions are met it must be made, and it repeats until no valid target is left in Range or the Tokens run out. If the target survives, the same Part must try again. Several units in Range Intercept in sequence, and a Missile Group's Units are each Intercepted on their own.

Each attempt spends one Token and is a Firing Action for all its bonuses and penalties, a Passive Intercept included (FAQ M26): the Caracal's reroll, Smoke and Low Profile all apply. Its own target rule stands: the target is the Unit that triggered it, Highlight never changes that, no Forward Arc is needed, and the target claims no Terrain or Unit Protection. Terrain never blocks a line to an Aerial Unit, but Smoke does (FAQ F3).

Fire Control Interference stops it, and so does Shutdown; a destroyed Part cannot Intercept. A Melee Locked Unit may still Intercept (ruled 2026-09-25). It neither Reveals a camouflaged interceptor nor removes a Low Profile Token (p.73). The Hyena Radar's {Eye} counts as a Light Hit for Interception alone (FAQ O12, O13).

mechanics.name: The End Phase
mechanics.basic: The last phase of each round, in four steps.
points: Remove units: every Mech with 2 or fewer Parts, and anything removed at the end of the round.
Tokens: remove red tokens, flip yellow ones, and remove every Command Token.
Score: check Tasks, award Victory Points and check for victory.
Pass the First Player Token, and start the next round.
mechanics.text:
Four steps, in this order.
- First remove units: every Mech left with 2 or fewer Parts goes, along with anything that says it is removed at the end of the round, alternating from the First Player if the order could matter.
- Second, token management: remove all Red Square and Hexagon Tokens, flip all Yellow ones to their reverse side, and remove every Command Token.
- Third, check Tasks, award Victory Points and test the victory conditions including the round limit.
- Fourth, flip the First Player Token so the other side goes first, and begin the next round.

A standard game runs five rounds, after which Victory Points are totalled.

mechanics.name: Building a squad
mechanics.basic: Build a squad up to an agreed points limit, from one faction.
points: The limits: 600 for a skirmish, 900 for a standard game, 1200 or more for a large one.
Every card costs its Points Value, and each Mech gets a Pilot.
A Mech's Parts and Pilot come from one faction, and RDL, UN and GoF do not mix in a squad.
Mercenary units (Planetring Dynamics, White Dwarf) may join any squad as whole units.
Two Pilots with the same ID cannot be in one squad.
mechanics.text:
Agree a points limit: 600 for a skirmish, 900 for a standard game, 1200 or more for a large one (5.1). Every card taken costs its Points Value against that total. Each Mech is assigned a Pilot, and two Pilots with the same ID cannot be in one squad.

A Mech is built entirely from one faction's Parts, and its Pilot is of that faction too. Across the squad RDL, UN and GoF do not mix. Planetring Dynamics and the White Dwarf collaboration are mercenaries: their Units may join an RDL, UN or GoF squad as complete Units, never as a Part on another faction's Mech. Tactics Cards are not bound by the faction rule (5.4.2).

A White Dwarf Bit, like every Low Value Unit, is not part of the Squad (p.82). The White Dwarf belongs to Ace Strategy: a Planetring Dynamics Mech cannot take its Parts (FAQ N6).

mechanics.name: Mines
mechanics.basic: A Mine sits in a Grid and explodes when a ground unit enters it. The blast catches everything there.
points: Any ground unit entering sets it off, ally or enemy, even one passing through, and a camouflaged one is not Revealed.
A unit already standing there when the Mine arrives does not set it off until it moves in again.
The blast hits every unit in the Grid, flying and Aerial ones too. Mines in one Grid go off together.
A Mine blocks nothing and is never Crushed. Flying units may land on it, and Melee may attack it.
The Mine Layer backpack Lays Mines along its own route for 1 Move Range each, or Deploys one within 1 Grid.
mechanics.text:
A Mine (the GM-35) detonates when a Ground Unit enters its Grid, whoever owns either (FAQ M6). Entering means moving in, being Knocked back or Crushed into it, or passing through: a unit walking through a mined Grid stops there, the blast resolves, and it goes on with the Range it has left unless its Chassis is destroyed (FAQ M19, I24; ruling I16). A camouflaged unit sets it off and is not Revealed.

A Mine placed where a Ground Unit already stands waits for a unit to enter (ruling I15). A Mine laid in the layer's own end Grid goes off as the layer enters it. Deploying a Mine into a Grid that holds one sets off the one that was there, and the new Mine is Deployed if that blast does not destroy it (FAQ M6).

The blast catches everything in the Grid, Flying and Aerial Units included (FAQ M22; ruling I17), and each Unit makes its own Attack and Defense Rolls. Mines in one Grid go off at the same time: they resolve one by one, and none destroys another (FAQ I13). The Mine's owner resolves the blast (4.7.6, p.64).

A Mine is its own kind of Unit (ruling I14):
- It blocks nothing, units may be placed above it, and it is never Crushed (FAQ E10).
- Flying Units may land on it, and a Flying or Aerial Unit never sets it off (FAQ M3, M24).
- Melee may target it, and it gets Protection like any other Unit (FAQ M10, M14).
- An enemy Mine placed in Contact with a camouflaged Unit ends the camouflage (FAQ I10).

Laying (FAQ M7, M29): the GLP-15's Auto Mine Laying spends 1 Move Range per Mine during the Mech's Movement and puts it in any Grid of the route, and a Flight Move's route is only its two ends. The Lay comes before the Crush, so a Mine laid ahead catches the unit the Crush pushes into it. The GLP-15 also Deploys one Mine within Range 1.

A Mine is a Low Value Unit (p.82), and an enemy one, never Neutral: a Drone's Automatic Action takes it before any Breakable Terrain (FAQ O10).

mechanics.name: Pholcus automatic mines
mechanics.basic: The Pholcus is Launched folded, then Unfolds into a Drone that hunts: it jumps to the nearest enemy and detonates.
points: It is launched like any Projectile, so it can be Intercepted, and it may land in an occupied Grid.
In the Delay Phase of that round it must Unfold into its Drone form.
Unfolding where a unit already stands sets it off at once, at one of them, ally or not.
From the next round it is a Drone. With an enemy in Range in the Automatic Phase, it must jump and detonate.
It is a Low Value Drone: destroying it scores nothing, and Crushing it causes no blast.
mechanics.ref: Card text (082, 156, 167); FAQ I10, M8, M18, M28, O10; rulings I18, I19
mechanics.text:
The SGM2 Pholcus Automatic Mine is Launched from the GSD2A Mine Rack as a Projectile with its own model, and it may be placed in an occupied Grid (FAQ M18.1, M18.2). It is a launch, so it is checked for Interception. The Rack never launches the Unfolded form. Landing in Contact with a camouflaged enemy ends the camouflage, as an enemy Deployable does (FAQ I10).

In the Delay Phase of the round it lands it must be replaced by its Unfolded Drone form (FAQ M18.3). If its Grid is occupied then, it detonates at once, even when the occupant is an ally (FAQ M18.4). Aerial Units and Mines are not occupants, and the blast takes one occupant, its owner choosing (rulings I18, I19). A unit sharing its Grid later sets nothing off.

The Unfolded Pholcus is a Drone from the next round and receives Commands (FAQ M18.5). In the Automatic Phase, with an enemy in its attack Range, it must jump to the nearest one and Detonate (FAQ M18.6), with no line of sight needed (FAQ M28). It cannot attack in the round it Unfolds, since the Automatic Phase comes before the Delay Phase (FAQ M8).

It is a Low Value Drone (FAQ M8): destroying it, or its own detonation, scores nothing, and a unit that Crushes it sets off no blast. Like every Mine it is an enemy Unit, never Neutral (FAQ O10).

mechanics.name: Loads
mechanics.basic: A Load is a Backpack a Carrier Tarantula carries, for the Mechs in Contact with it to use.
points: Only the Carrier Tarantula carries a Load, only a Backpack can be one, and some Backpacks never can.
The Carrier never uses its Load: it gains none of the Part's Actions or attributes.
A Mech in Contact may use the Load as its own Part while it acts: its Actions, bonuses, Dodge and Freehand.
Two Carriers lend two separate Parts, and their bonuses stack. Ammo spent comes off the Carrier.
A Load is its Carrier's faction, and it costs its Points like any Part.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook p.94; FAQ N6, O3-O8, O16-O18; rulings I24-I27
mechanics.text:
The ADK30C Tarantula Carrier Type carries one Backpack as its Load, or none (FAQ O8). Only a Backpack can be a Load, and several Backpacks print that they never can, the EBS/X40 among them (FAQ O18). A Load is a Part of the Carrier's faction (5.1, FAQ N6; ruling I26), and it costs its Points like any Part.

The Carrier does not gain the Load's Actions or attributes: it carries it, and never uses it (p.94). A Carrier holding an Electronic Warfare Backpack adds nothing to its own Counter-roll (FAQ O4).

An Ally Mech in Contact with the Carrier may regard the Load as its own Part when it performs Actions (FAQ O3, O16): its Actions, its passive bonuses, its Electronic Value, Dodge Value and Freehand. The Mech's own Backpack still works beside it, and two Carriers' Coolers stack on one Firing Action (FAQ O17). Two Carriers lend two separate Parts, so the same Action may be used once from each (FAQ O7).

The loan counts only while the Mech acts. A borrowed Electronic Value counts when the Mech Initiates a Counter-roll, never when it Responds (FAQ O5, O6), and a borrowed Dodge only when the Mech is attacked during its own Action, such as by a Mine it sets off (ruling I24). Ammo spent from a borrowed Part comes off the Carrier. A Mech in Contact may Intercept with a lent AMS, paying from the Carrier's Tokens (ruling I25).

A Load's Freehand serves [Two-Handed] alone: a Black Box is never picked up with it (ruling I27).

mechanics.name: The White Dwarf
mechanics.basic: The White Dwarf is a transforming Mech: it flies in Cruise Mode, and launches Bits from its Bit Port.
points: It Transforms between its Mech form and Cruise Mode, and may deploy in either.
In Cruise Mode it is in Mobility, always flying, and only its Torso acts or takes the hits.
Cruising, it sets off no Mines, is never Melee Locked and Locks nobody.
Its Bits are one Aerial Drone printed on three Stance cards, launched and recovered by the Bit Port.
A Bit keeps its Tokens when it changes Stance, and a recovered Bit comes back as a new unit.
mechanics.ref: Collab 1.02 (Ace Strategy) additional rules; Rulebook p.82; FAQ M24, N1-N8; rulings I23, I28, I29
mechanics.text:
The White Dwarf (Ace Strategy) Transforms between its Mech form and Cruise Mode, turning its Parts over to their other faces. It may be deployed in either mode, and deployed in Cruise Mode it is in Mobility Stance (ruling I28).

In Cruise Mode:
- Upon entering it, the Mech switches to Mobility Stance, and no other Stance may be selected.
- It is always a Flying Unit: it may enter a mined Grid and sets off no Mine (FAQ M24).
- No hit location is determined, and the Torso takes the hit. Scatter-shot's Surplus still reaches another Part, and Cleaving's too (FAQ N7; ruling I29).
- Only the Torso acts, unless an Action says it may be used in Cruise Mode. A lent Load acts no more than an arm.
- Suppression does not affect it, and it neither Melee Locks nor is Melee Locked (FAQ N3).
- With Freehand it may take a Black Box, and it keeps one it already carries (FAQ N1, N2).

The Bits:
- A "White Dwarf" Bit is one Drone printed on three cards, one per Stance. It is an Aerial Unit (FAQ N5) and a Low Value Unit, never part of the Squad (p.82).
- The Bit Port Launches one in any Stance within Range 6, spending its Ammo Token, or Recovers one within Range 6, restoring the Token (ruling I23). A Launch is checked for Interception.
- A Bit's Stance Change turns its card over and keeps everything on it, its Command Token included, so it cannot take another Command (FAQ N8).
- A recovered Bit leaves play, and one launched again is a new unit with none of its old Tokens (FAQ N4, N8).
- The Thruster: while the Bit Port holds its Ammo Token, a {Lightning} on the Blue dice may be exchanged for {Dodge}.

The White Dwarf belongs to Ace Strategy: it is Neutral and joins any squad as a whole Unit, but its Parts never go on a Planetring Dynamics Mech (FAQ N6).

mechanics.name: What an Automatic Attack Must Shoot
mechanics.basic: An Automatic attack must shoot the nearest enemy it may target, and the Drone must take it.
points: Firing and Melee ones count only enemies in sight, and in the Forward Arc unless Omni-directional.
A Highlighted enemy comes first for Firing, and a Target Tracer lets a Drone take a bearer farther off.
Range counts Large Grids in straight lines, so a diagonal neighbour is 2 away. A tie is the controller's choice.
Melee never targets an Aerial unit, and a Melee reach of "--" is the Adjacent Grids, diagonals included.
With no enemy in Range, it may shoot the nearest Breakable Terrain it could target instead.
mechanics.text:
An Automatic Action targets the nearest enemy Unit it may target (3.5.2), and it is obligatory: a Drone with a legal target must take it (3.5; ruling I4). For a Firing or Melee Action the enemies counted are those within the Action's Range and line of sight, and only those in its Forward Arc unless the Action is Omni-directional (4.2.5). Range is counted across Large Grids, not diagonally, so a diagonal neighbour is 2 away. A tie is the controller's choice.

What changes the pick:
- Highlight binds Firing Actions only (FAQ J18): if an enemy counted bears a Highlight Token, the nearest Highlighted one is taken (FAQ O21).
- A Target Tracer lets a Drone take its bearer even when it is not the nearest (6.3.3).
- An Electronic Attack may be measured from an allied Repeater, and the nearest is then counted from there (FAQ O19, O20).
- The Unit types a card names limit what it may take.
- Melee never targets an Aerial Unit, and a Melee Action printing "--" reaches the Adjacent Grids, diagonals included (4.2.2).
- The Unfolded Pholcus needs no line of sight for its jump (FAQ M28).

If no enemy is in Range, the Action may instead target the nearest Neutral Unit it could target: a 1-inch Breakable Terrain container in sight, in the arc and within any lengthened Range (FAQ O9; ruling I5). Buildings and Defense Walls are never valid targets. Beacons and Mines are enemy Units, never Neutral, so they are targeted before Breakable Terrain (FAQ O10).

mechanics.name: Smoke Screens
mechanics.basic: Smoke Screens block line of sight for Firing Actions, though any clear line around them still works.
points: A Firing Action may attack along any line between the bases that crosses no Smoke and no 3-inch terrain.
A unit in a Grid with Smoke cannot fire, or be fired at, with Firing Actions. Aerial units are no exception.
Smoke stops Interception too, but not Melee or Projectile Actions, nor effects that only need a unit to be visible.
Smoke gives no Terrain Protection, and a player may have only one Smoke Screen in a Grid.
Once each End Phase, Smoke thins: lone cards go, and one card from each connected group.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook 4.16; FAQ B7, D10, F1-F5, M26
mechanics.text:
Smoke Screens are placed when a Smoke Grenade detonates, or by an ability such as Emergency Smoke, and are represented by Smoke Screen Cards. The GS-2 Smoke Grenade has no model and detonates the moment it lands. A Smoke Screen is placed within a Grid, never across Large Grids, and may share a Grid with Units or Terrain.

When an Action places several at once, its text may require them to be Connected: each one must share an edge with at least one other placed by that Action, and a corner touch does not connect (4.2.3). The card's Black or White side shows which player placed it. Smoke Screens placed by the same player cannot overlap in one Grid; those placed by different players can.

Line of sight cannot be established through a Smoke Screen for a Firing Action. If the Attacker can draw line of sight along any line between the bases that does not pass through the Smoke, it may attack as normal (4.16, 4.2.4). Smoke and 3-inch terrain are judged on the same lines: a line that crosses either is blocked, and one clear line is enough. This affects both players equally, whoever placed the Smoke.

- A Unit in the same Grid as a Smoke Screen cannot establish line of sight to or from anything for Firing Actions. Aerial Units are no exception, whether in the Smoke or looking through it: Smoke counts as infinitely high (FAQ F1, F2).
- Interception is a Firing Action (FAQ M26), so Smoke stops it too: a Projectile whose starting or landing Grid is in Smoke cannot be Intercepted there (F3), and neither can an interceptor standing in or looking through Smoke. The Hyena's AA Radar still works (F5).
- Smoke does not give Terrain Protection (FAQ F4).
- Actions other than Firing Actions, such as Melee and Projectile Actions, are not affected, a Direct Fire Action's sight of its Landing Point included (FAQ F1). Nor are effects that only ask whether a Unit is visible, such as Early Warning, Tracking and Target Tag (FAQ F5; ruled 2026-09-25).

Emergency Smoke from a Multi-Target Action is placed after the last of its attacks (FAQ B7), and a Unit the attack destroyed places none (FAQ D10).

Dissipation happens once in each End Phase: each player removes all of their Smoke Screens that are not Connected, and one Smoke Screen from each of their Connected groups, the players alternating. Connected here means the same player's Smoke Screens sharing an edge. If a placement joins two groups into one, only one card is removed from the merged group. If a removal splits a group in two, the two groups owe no further removal that round; in the following round's End Phase one is removed from each.

mechanics.name: Black Boxes
mechanics.basic: A Task Item worth Victory Points in the missions that use it.
points: Pick it up by moving through it, or by ending an Action Opportunity in its Grid, using a Part with the Freehand tag.
That Part's Freehand then counts as used.
A bearer that is Penetrated drops it, and the attacker places it touching the bearer.
It blocks neither Line of Sight nor Movement.
mechanics.text:
A Task Item worth Victory Points in the missions built around it (5.3.1). On the board it occupies 1 small Grid, may overlap Units, and blocks neither Line of Sight nor Movement.

A Unit picks one up by moving through its position or by ending an Action Opportunity in its Grid, using a Part with the Freehand tag; that Freehand then counts as occupied. The token is placed on the Part or Unit Card that holds it. A bearer that is Penetrated drops the Black Box: the Attacker places it in contact with the bearer's base.

Scoring is per Main Task card, which may require the box to be held in a named zone at a named time.

mechanics.name: Overwatch
mechanics.basic: The KK9 Snake Eyes' Overwatch Strike names an enemy, and an ally Mech fires at it at once.
points: The KK9 performs it as a Command Action, naming 1 enemy within its Range.
One ally Mech then performs 1 Firing Action at that enemy, and at no other, straight away.
The Firing Action may be of any length, but it is one Action, and it costs the Mech no Ticks.
Then the KK9 is removed.
mechanics.ref: Card text (LHDR-KK9, TM39D); FAQ K15; ruling I8
mechanics.text:
The KK9 Snake Eyes Micro Drone, which the TM39D Cobra launches, carries Overwatch Strike, a Command Action: designate 1 enemy Unit within its Range as the target, and 1 Ally Mech may immediately perform 1 Firing Action against it. Then the KK9 is removed. The shooter need not be the Mech that launched it.

The Firing Action belongs to the card, not to an Action Opportunity, so it costs no Ticks. It may be Short, Medium or Long, but it is one Action (FAQ K15), and it may be made at the designated enemy alone.

mechanics.name: Repeaters and AA radar
mechanics.basic: Two Drone abilities: a Repeater passes on Electronic Warfare, and the Hyena's AA Radar helps allies shoot at Aerial targets.
points: An ally within a Repeater's Range may measure an Electronic Attack or Electronic Support from the Repeater instead of from itself.
One Repeater per Action. A Scan or Remote Access cannot use one.
AA Radar: when allies Intercept a target this Drone can see, they may count Eyes as Light Hits.
AA Radar is always on, works only for Interception, and is not stopped by Smoke.
mechanics.ref: Official FAQ G1, G2, O12, O13, O19, O20, P12, F5; card 165
mechanics.text:
A Repeater (the Raven EC's has Range 6) lets an allied unit within that Range measure an Electronic Attack or Electronic Support from the Repeater instead of from itself: the Action's own Range is then counted from the Repeater (FAQ O19).

- One Repeater per Action (FAQ G1), and Drones may use one too (FAQ G2).
- An Automatic Electronic Attack sent through one takes the target nearest the Repeater (FAQ O20).
- A Strength +X bonus does not travel through the Raven EC (card 165), and Remote Access and Scan cannot use a Repeater at all (FAQ P12).

The Hyena's AA Radar reads "When Ally Units Intercept targets that are visible to this drone, they may exchange Eye for Light Hit". It is always active (FAQ O12), applies to Interception only (FAQ O13), and still works in or through Smoke (FAQ F5).

mechanics.name: Contact
mechanics.basic: Two units are in Contact when their bases touch edge to edge.
points: It is measured on the Small Grids they occupy, not the Large Grid.
Touching only corner to corner is Adjacent, but not Contact.
Overlapping bases count as Contact, like a Mine or an Aerial unit over a ground unit.
A Movement ending in Contact Reveals a camouflaged unit. Contact never removes a Low Profile Token.
Terrain in Contact with the attacker gives the target no Protection.
mechanics.ref: Rulebook 4.2.3; FAQ A1, I4, I24, J19, L7
mechanics.text:
Two Units or Terrain Objects are in Contact when at least one edge of the Small Grids they occupy overlaps (4.2.3). It is measured on the footprints, not the Large Grid.

Contact differs from Adjacent: a corner-to-corner touch is Adjacent but not Contact, and two Units sharing a Large Grid are always Adjacent but in Contact only if their footprints touch.

Overlapping bases, a Mine or an Aerial Unit placed above another Unit, count as Contact and as Adjacent. That comes from the Rules Supplement's rule for overlapping, as FAQ I24 and L7 quote it; the rulebook itself does not say it.

Contact is what an enemy needs to Reveal a Unit in Optical Camouflage, and only when a Movement ends in it (FAQ I4). It never removes a Low Profile Token (FAQ J19). A Carrier Tarantula needs it before it lends its Load, and Terrain in Contact with the attacker gives the target no Terrain Protection (FAQ A1). A card that says adjacent means Adjacent, not Contact.

mechanics.name: Adjacent
mechanics.basic: A unit in any of the eight Large Grids around another, diagonals included, is Adjacent to it.
points: Two units sharing a Large Grid are Adjacent too.
An Action with Range "--" can only target Adjacent units, and still only in its Forward Arc.
A card that says adjacent means this, diagonals included: not Contact, and not Range 1.
Adjacent is looser than Contact, which needs the bases themselves to touch.
mechanics.text:
The eight Large Grids surrounding the one a Unit stands in are its Adjacent Grids, diagonals included, and a Unit standing in any of them is Adjacent to it. Small and Medium Units may share a Large Grid, and two Units sharing one are Adjacent as well. A Range of "--" on an Action means it can only target Adjacent Units, and a "--" attack still needs its target in the Forward Arc (FAQ A9).

Range counts orthogonal steps between Large Grids (4.2.1), so a diagonal neighbour is Adjacent and at Range 2: a "--" Action reaches it, and a Range 1 Action does not. A card printing "adjacent" means Adjacent, diagonals included: the Harpy's tow of an adjacent Ally and the RKG70's resupply of an adjacent Ally Unit both reach a diagonal neighbour, and neither needs Contact.

Adjacent is the looser of the game's two proximity terms: it is measured in whole Large Grids and counts diagonals, where Contact is measured on the Small Grid edges and does not.

mechanics.name: Tether
mechanics.basic: A Tether binds a target to the unit that landed it: the tethered unit cannot move more than X Grids from it.
points: Only the tethered unit is held, in every move of its own, a Manifestation or a controlled move included.
It never stops an Action. The Grids past the leash cannot even be passed through.
It ends if the tethering unit moves or Blinks beyond X, is Penetrated or destroyed, or either is pushed past X.
While it holds, Link Shock hits the tethered unit at any distance, but still needs the Forward Arc.
mechanics.ref: Card text: PDLH-202 and PDRH-202 (the keyword has no rulebook appendix entry)
mechanics.text:
Tether X binds two Units: a Tether X Token on the Unit that landed it, a Tethered X Token on the target. The initiating Unit may move freely. The Tether is not a cost and never prevents an Action.

Only the tethered Unit is restrained: it cannot voluntarily move further than X grids from the initiating Unit, not even in passing, since the Grids beyond are closed to its route. That holds for every Movement of its own, a Manifestation from Optical Camouflage and a move The Red Shoes steers it through included, since neither is Forced Movement (ruled 2026-09-25).

Both Tokens are removed when any of these happens: the initiating Unit voluntarily moves beyond X grids, a Blink included; the initiating Unit is Penetrated; either Unit is forcibly moved so the distance ends up greater than X; or either Unit is destroyed or leaves the table. Distance is checked after anything that moves either Unit.

The Ols1B Harpoon swaps to its Tether Mode face while the Tether holds, which offers nothing but Harpoon Retrieve, and back when it ends, including when its Hit destroyed the target and left nothing to hold. Its Range 4 makes it Extended Melee, which needs line of sight (4.6.2).

The Ot130L's Link Shock may only target a Unit this Mech has Tethered, ignoring distance and line of sight, and the target cannot Parry, choose the hit location or roll Blue Dice. It keeps the Forward Arc and the rule that a Melee Action cannot target an Aerial Unit (ruled 2026-09-25). (Card text: PDLH-202 and PDRH-202; the keyword has no rulebook appendix entry.)
